  • Computer Science (C S)

Computer Science (C S)

C S 301K  Foundations of Logical Thought  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Introductory logic in the context of computing; introduction to formal notations; basic proof techniques; sets, relations, and functions. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Some sections also require one discussion hour a week.
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 302  Computer Fluency  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
An introduction to the fundamental concepts of computing: how computers work, what they can do, and how they can be used effectively. Some programming is required. Credit for Computer Science 302 may not be earned after a student has received credit for Computer Science 303E, 312, 312H, 314, or 314H. May not be counted toward a degree in computer science. Three lecture hours or two lecture hours and one discussion hour a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 093  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 303E  Elements of Computers and Programming  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Problem solving and fundamental algorithms for various applications in science, business, and on the World Wide Web, and introductory programming in a modern object-oriented programming language. Only one of the following may be counted: Computer Science 303E, 312, 312H. Credit for Computer Science 303E may not be earned after a student has received credit for Computer Science 314, or 314H. May not be counted toward a degree in computer science. The equivalent of three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 093  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 103F  Ethical Foundations of Computer Science  1 Hour  

1 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
An introduction to reasoning about the effects of the technology created by computer scientists and understanding the ethical and real-world consequences of that technology. Emphasizes direct participation and discussion using case studies to illustrate ethical topics. Computer Science 103F and 109 (Topic: Ethical Foundations of Computer Science) may not both be counted. One lecture hour a week for one semester.
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 104C  Competitive Programming  1 Hour  

1 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Explores the algorithms needed to solve a given problem, reason about corner cases, and write correct implementations under time pressure. Focuses on skills useful for international programming competitions, whiteboard job interviews, and programming tasks that require quickly solving challenging problems with creative use of algorithms. Computer Science 104 and 109 (Topic: Competitive Programming) may not both be counted. One lecture hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 311 or 311H with a grade of at least C-, and registration or credit in Computer Science 314 or 314H with a grade of at least C-.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 304I  Essentials of AI for Life and Society  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Examine fundamental concepts for AI literacy, as well as the ethical and societal implications of AI technologies. Only one of the following may be counted: Computer Science 304I, 109 (Topic: Essentials of AI: Life/Soc), 309 (Topic: AI Literacy: Essent of AI). Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 093  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 105C  Computer Programming: C++  1 Hour  

1 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Explores the syntax and concepts needed to program in C++. One lecture hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 313E, 314, 314H, or Electrical Engineering 422C, with a grade of at least C-.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 105P  Topics In Computer Programming Languages  1 Hour  

1 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
An introduction to programming in a particular computer language. Includes designing and implementing programs. One lecture hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 313E, 314, 314H, or Electrical Engineering 422C, with a grade of at least C-, and consent of instructor.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 108  Topics in Software Systems  1 Hour  

1 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Introduction to the use of a particular software system. Students build applications that exploit the system being studied. One lecture hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 313E, 314, 314H, or Electrical Engineering 422C, with a grade of at least C-.  
Grading: Pass/Fail  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 109, 209, 309  Topics in Computer Science  1-3 Hours  

1,2,3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
For each semester hour of credit earned, one lecture hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Varies with the topic.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  
Academic Level: Lower Division  
Topic 1: Quantum Computing I. Introduction to quantum information and communication. Computer Science 309 (Topic: Quantum Computing-FRI) and 309 (Topic 1) may not both be counted.
  

C S 109.1, 209.1, 309.1  Quantum Computing I  1-3 Hours  

1,2,3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Introduction to quantum information and communication. Computer Science 309 (Topic: Quantum Computing-FRI) and 309 (Topic 1) may not both be counted.
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 311  Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
A focus on discrete mathematical tools of fundamental importance to the working computer scientist. An emphasis is placed on using logical notation to express rigorous mathematical arguments. Subjects include proof by induction, introduction to graph theory, recurrences, sets, functions, and an introduction to program correctness. Computer Science 311 and 311H may not both be counted. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: The following coursework with a grade of at least C- in each: Computer Science 312 or 312H; and Mathematics 408C, 408K, or 408N, or registration for Mathematics 408C.  
Restrictions: Restricted to computer science majors.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 311H  Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science: Honors  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
A focus on discrete mathematical tools of fundamental importance to the working computer scientist. An emphasis is placed on using logical notation to express rigorous mathematical arguments. Subjects include proof by induction, graph theory, number theory, combinatorics, recurrences, sets, functions, an introduction to program correctness, and discrete probability. Computer Science 311 and 311H may not both be counted. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Mathematics 408K or 408N with a grade of at least C-; or registration or credit with at least C- in M 408C.  
Restrictions: Restricted to honors computer science majors.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 312  Introduction to Programming  3 Hours  

4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
First part of a two-part sequence in programming. Fundamental concepts of structured programming; procedures and data structures with a focus on problem solving strategies and implementation; introduction to concepts of informal specification, informal reasoning about program behavior, debugging, and ad hoc testing. Only one of the following courses may be counted: Computer Science 303E, 312, 312H. Credit for Computer Science 312 may not be earned after a student has received credit for Computer Science 314 or 314H. Three lecture hours and one discussion hour a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 093  
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Mathematics 408C, 408K, or 408N.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 312H  Introduction to Programming: Honors  3 Hours  

4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
First part of a two-part sequence in programming. Fundamental concepts of structured programming; procedures and data structures with a focus on problem solving strategies and implementation; introduction to concepts of informal specification, informal reasoning about program behavior, debugging, and ad hoc testing. Only one of the following courses may be counted: Computer Science 303E, 312, 312H. Credit for Computer Science 312H may not be earned after a student has received credit for Computer Science 314 or 314H. Three lecture hours and one discussion hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Mathematics 305G, or a passing score on the College of Natural Sciences mathematics placement examination; and consent of the honors director.  
Restrictions: Restricted to computer science majors.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 313E  Elements of Software Design  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Object-oriented design of software using Python, a modern high-level language. Introduction to abstract data types, fundamental algorithms, and basics of complexity analysis. May not be counted toward a degree in computer science. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 303E, 312, or 312H with a grade of at least C-.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 314  Data Structures  3 Hours  

4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Second part of a two-part sequence in programming. Introduction to specifications, simple unit testing, and debugging; building and using canonical data structures; algorithm analysis and reasoning techniques such as assertions and invariants. Computer Science 314 and 314H may not both be counted. Three lecture hours and one discussion hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 312 or 312H with a grade of at least C-.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 314H  Data Structures: Honors  3 Hours  

4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Second part of a two-part sequence in programming. Introduction to specifications, simple unit testing, and debugging; building and using canonical data structures; algorithm analysis and reasoning techniques such as assertions and invariants. Computer Science 314 and 314H may not both be counted. Three lecture hours and one discussion hour a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 093  
Pre/Corequisites: Consent of honors faculty advisor.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 118H  Introduction to Computer Science Research: Honors  1 Hour  

1 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Introduction to computer science research. Discuss various aspects of undergraduate research, including the benefits of undergraduate research, ways to get started in undergraduate research, the mechanics and expectations of an undergraduate honors thesis, and tips to help have a successful undergraduate research experience. Computer Science 118H and 178H (Topic: Intro to Comp Sci Rsch: Honors) may not both be counted. One lecture hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Consent of instructor.  
Restrictions: Restricted to computer science honors students.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

C S 119S, 219S, 319S, 419S, 519S, 619S, 719S, 819S, 919S  Topics in Computer Science  1-9 Hours  

0 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
This course is used to record credit the student earns while enrolled at another institution in a program administered by the University's Study Abroad Office. Credit is recorded as assigned by the study abroad adviser in the Department of Computer Science. University credit is awarded for work in an exchange program; it may be counted as coursework taken in residence. Transfer credit is awarded for work in an affiliated studies program.
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  

C S 120N, 220N, 320N  Topics in Computer Science for Nonmajors  1-3 Hours  

1,2,3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
May not be counted toward a degree in computer science. For each semester hour of credit earned, one lecture hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Varies with the topic.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

C S 323E  Elements of Scientific Computing  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Explore the fundamentals of software issues related to scientific computing. Discuss subjects including floating-point computations, numerical computation errors, interpolation, integration, solution of linear systems of equations, optimization, and initial value problems of ordinary differential equations. Examine implementation of algorithms that are investigated using Python for all scientific computations. Computer Science 323E and 323H may not both be counted. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: The following with a grade of at least C-: Computer Science 313E, 314, or 314H; and Mathematics 408C, 408K, 408N, 408Q or 408R.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

C S 323H  Elements of Scientific Computing: Honors  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Fundamentals of software issues related to scientific computing. Subjects include floating-point computations, numerical computation errors, interpolation, integration, solution of linear systems of equations, optimization, and initial value problems of ordinary differential equations. Implementation of algorithms are investigated using MATLAB for matrix and vector computations. Examples are drawn from a variety of science and mathematics areas. May not be counted toward a degree in computer science. Computer Science 323E and 323H may not both be counted. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 303E, 312, or 312H with a grade of at least C-; credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Mathematics 340L, or 341; and consent of the honors director.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

C S 324E  Elements of Graphics and Visualization  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Basics of two- and three-dimensional computer graphics systems, modeling and rendering, and selected graphics software APIs. Other topics may include interactive graphics, animation, graphical user interfaces, and the graphical presentation of information. May not be counted toward a degree in computer science. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 313E, 314, or 314H with a grade of at least C-.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

C S 326E  Elements of Networking  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Introduction to the principles and basic concepts of the Internet, networking applications and protocols, and simple client/server applications. Other topics may include network technologies and topologies, packet and circuit switching, LANS and WANS, Internet security, and network management. May not be counted toward a degree in computer science. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 313E, 314, or 314H with a grade of at least C-.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

C S 327E  Elements of Databases  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
A practical introduction to database management systems, with discussion of database administration and management. Survey of logical modeling, database design with a focus on relational databases, SQL query language, and current applications. Subjects may include data integrity, performance, concurrency, transaction processing, recovery, security, and Web applications. May not be counted toward a degree in computer science. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 313E, 314, or 314H with a grade of at least C-.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

C S 328E  Topics in Elements of Computing  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
May not be counted toward a degree in computer science. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 303E, 312, or 312H with a grade of at least C-.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

C S 429  Computer Organization and Architecture  4 Hours  

6 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
An introduction to low-level computer design ranging from the basics of digital design to the hardware/software interface for application programs. Includes basic systems principles of pipelining and caching, and requires writing and understanding programs at multiple levels. Computer Science 429 and 429H may not both be counted. Four lecture hours and two discussion hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: The following courses with a grade of at least C-: Computer Science 311 or 311H; and Computer Science 314 or 314H.  
Restrictions: Restricted to computer science majors.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

C S 329E  Advanced Topics in Elements of Computing  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
May not be counted toward a degree in computer science. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Computer Science 313E, 314, or 314H with a grade of at least C-.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

C S 429H  Computer Organization and Architecture: Honors  4 Hours  

6 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
An introduction to low-level computer design ranging from the basics of digital design to the hardware/software interface for application programs. Includes basic systems principles of pipelining and caching, and requires writing and understanding programs at multiple levels. Only one of the following may be counted: Computer Science 310, 310H, 429, 429H. Four lecture hours and two discussion hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: The following coursework with a grade of at least C- in each: Computer Science 311 or 311H; Computer Science 314 or 314H.  
Restrictions: Restricted to computer science majors.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

C S 129S, 229S, 329S, 429S, 529S, 629S, 729S, 829S, 929S  Topics in Computer Science  1-9 Hours  

0 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
This course is used to record credit the student earns while enrolled at another institution in a program administered by the University's Study Abroad Office. Credit is recorded as assigned by the study abroad adviser in the Department of Computer Science. University credit is awarded for work in an exchange program; it may be counted as coursework taken in residence. Transfer credit is awarded for work in an affiliated studies program.
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  

C S 329W  Cooperative Computer Science  3 Hours  

0 Lecture Hours  40 Lab Hours  
This course covers the work period of computer science students in the Cooperative Education program, which provides supervised work experience by arrangement with the employer and the supervising instructor. The student must repeat the course each work period and must take it twice to receive credit toward the degree; at least one of these registrations must be during a fall or spring semester. However, no more than three semester hours may be counted toward the major requirement. The student's first registration must be on the pass/fail basis; the second must be on the letter-grade basis. Forty laboratory hours a week for one semester.

C S 386C  Dependable Computing Systems  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
System models from synchronous to asynchronous, with emphasis on in-between models such as the timed asynchronous model. Control structures such as timed state-transition systems, and constraints in temporal and real-time logics. Analysis techniques such as model checking of timed systems, and extended Presburger arithmetic. Basic building blocks such as clock synchronization, synchronous atomic broadcast, time-bounded membership protocols, real-time scheduling theory, and state recovery methods. Practical implementation issues such as special operating system data structures and algorithms, open system design, and security concerns. Computer Science 386C and 395T (Topic: Dependable Computing Systems) may not both be counted. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing, and an undergraduate course in operating systems or consent of instructor.

Restrictions: Open only to those in their first two years as graduate students in computer science.  
Grading: Credit No Credit  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Doctoral  

C S 396M  Advanced Networking Protocols  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Topics include routing, multiple access, internetworking, security, performance models, and verification methods. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Doctoral  

C S 698  Thesis  6 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
The equivalent of three lecture hours a week for two semesters.
Pre/Corequisites: For 698A, graduate standing in computer science and consent of the graduate adviser; for 698B, Computer Science 698A.  
Grading: Credit No Credit  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Master's  

C S 398T  Supervised Teaching in Computer Science  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Supervised teaching experience, and seminar focused on curriculum construction and teaching methods. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing and appointment as a teaching assistant.  
Grading: Credit No Credit  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Doctoral  

C S 399W, 699W, 999W  Dissertation  3,6,9 Hours  

0 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Pre/Corequisites: Admission to candidacy for the doctoral degree.  
Grading: Credit No Credit  
Repeatable for credit: Yes (Unlimited)  
Academic Level: Doctoral
